claims.text: GPT-4-based TrialGPT-Retrieval achieves an average recall of 86.2% at top 500 retrieved clinical trials across three patient cohorts.
GPT-4-based TrialGPT-Retrieval selects 5.5% of the initial document collection on average to recall at least 90% of relevant clinical trials.
TrialGPT-Matching achieves a criterion-level eligibility prediction accuracy of 87.3% on manual evaluation of 1015 patient-criterion pairs.
TrialGPT-Matching generates correct relevance explanations in 87.8% of evaluated patient-criterion pairs.
TrialGPT-Matching sentence location predictions achieve 90.1% precision, 87.9% recall, and an F1 score of 88.6%.
GPT-4-based TrialGPT-Ranking using feature combination achieves an NDCG@10 of 0.7275 for ranking candidate clinical trials.
GPT-4-based TrialGPT-Ranking using feature combination achieves an AUROC of 0.7979 for excluding ineligible clinical trials.
TrialGPT reduces screening time by 42.6% overall in a clinical trial patient recruitment user study.
Prior dense retrieval neural models for patient-trial matching require large datasets that are often infeasible to acquire due to missing paired annotations.

evidence.description: Overall, the average recall at the top 500 retrieved clinical trials is 50.0%, 83.4%, 86.2% for the raw note, TrialGPT-Retrieval with GPT-3.5, and TrialGPT-Retrieval with GPT-4, respectively.

On average, to recall at least 90% of the relevant clinical trials, GPT-4-based TrialGPT-Retrieval only needs to select 5.5% of the initial document collection, and GPT-3.5-based TrialGPT-Retrieval needs 7.0%.
Manual evaluations on 1015 patient-criterion pairs show that TrialGPT-Matching achieves an accuracy of 87.3% with faithful explanations, close to the expert performance.
Overall, most explanations are 'correct' (87.8%) by manual evaluations, while less than 10% of explanations are 'partially correct' (9.66%), and only a small proportion are 'incorrect' (2.56%).
The TrialGPT-predicted sentence locations are 90.1% correct (precision) and cover 87.9% of the ground-truth relevant sentence IDs (recall), leading to an F1 score of 88.6%.
Combining both linear and LLM aggregations yields the highest NDCG@10 performance of 0.7275 and the P@10 of 0.6699 for GPT-4-based TrialGPT-Ranking.
Both GPT-3.5-based and GPT-4-based TrialGPT-Ranking outperforms all baselines, and the combination of the features achieves an AUROC of 0.6582 and 0.7979, respectively.
The overall time saving for all patient-trial pairs is about 42.6%, which shows its great potential to enhance the efficiency of the clinical trial matching process.

Nonetheless, training neural networks with the language understanding capability of criteria texts and patient records requires large datasets. This is often infeasible due to the lack of paired patient-criterion matching annotations.

methodologies.name: TrialGPT
methodologies.description: An end-to-end LLM-driven patient-to-trial matching framework consisting of keyword-based hybrid-fusion candidate retrieval (TrialGPT-Retrieval), criterion-level patient eligibility prediction and explanation generation (TrialGPT-Matching), and trial-level eligibility score aggregation and candidate ranking (TrialGPT-Ranking).

limitations.text: Prior neural dense retrieval models for patient-trial matching rely on large paired datasets that are often unavailable and produce non-explainable outputs.
TrialGPT relies on OpenAI's GPT series LLMs, which are closed-source and accessible only through commercial APIs.
The evaluation did not test long longitudinal clinical notes, structured EHR data, lab values, imaging, or administrative criteria such as geolocation and trial recruitment status.
The pilot user study evaluating screening time reduction had a limited sample size.

future_work.text: Explore using and fine-tuning open-source LLMs as alternatives to closed-source commercial LLMs.
Explore alternative prompting strategies for each component of the TrialGPT framework.
Investigate how TrialGPT performs when integrating longitudinal clinical notes, structured data, and multi-modal inputs from electronic health records (EHRs).
Conduct larger-scale prospective evaluations regarding the impact of LLM-assisted clinical workflows in prospective trial matching settings.
